---
title: "Agentic AI Engineering Bootcamp"
subtitle: "3-Day Hands-on Intensive: Architecture, Orchestration, Tooling & Production Governance"
---

### Program Overview

This intensive, three-day hands-on bootcamp equips **entry-level software engineers, technical leads, and computer science students with foundational LLM programming experience** with the practical skills needed to design, build, evaluate, and safely operate autonomous, tool-using agentic systems.

Participants transition from basic, single-turn prompt-and-response scripts to stateful, multi-turn agent graphs, interoperable tool protocols (**Model Context Protocol - MCP**), modular agent skills, rigorous regression testing, and production-grade observability.

::: {.callout-note}
### Quick Facts
- **Audience:** Entry-level software engineers and university students with LLM programming fundamentals.
- **Duration:** 3 Days &middot; 12 Deep-Dive Sessions &middot; 10 Guided Hands-on Labs &middot; 1 Capstone Showcase.
- **Pacing:** 40% Architecture & Design Principles, 60% Practical Guided Labs.
- **Default Model:** Google Gemini (`gemini-2.5-flash` / `gemini-1.5-pro`) via the official `google-genai` SDK.
- **Tooling Standards:** Python 3.11+ managed with **`uv`**, Node.js 22 LTS with **`npm`**, and zero-friction local telemetry.
- **Interactive Slide Deck:** [Launch Agentic AI Bootcamp Presentation](../tech/agentic-ai/index.html){target="_blank"}
:::

---

### Prerequisites

1. **Python Programming:** Comfort with Python functions, classes, async syntax, dictionaries, and virtual environments.
2. **LLM Fundamentals:** Working understanding of prompts, completions, tokens, temperature, and making API calls to LLMs.
3. **Developer Tooling:** Basic comfort with terminal CLI commands, Git (`clone`, `commit`, `branch`), and VS Code.

---

### Overall Learning Outcomes

By completing the bootcamp, participants will be able to:

1. **Differentiate Agentic Systems:** Explain what makes a system agentic versus a standard LLM pipeline or chatbot, placing any architecture accurately on the autonomy spectrum.
2. **Design Agent Runtimes:** Architect agents from first principles (foundation model, instructions, context engineering, tool contracts, memory, and reasoning loops).
3. **Master Production Frameworks:** Implement stateful workflows and approval gates in both **LangGraph** and the **Google Gen AI Agent Development Kit (ADK)** using Gemini models.
4. **Standardize Tooling with MCP:** Build and connect custom servers using the open **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** across local `stdio` and HTTP transports.
5. **Package Reusable Agent Skills:** Author, test, and distribute modular skill bundles with progressive disclosure to keep prompt contexts lean.
6. **Accelerate with Coding Agents:** Direct CLI coding agents using spec-driven development, test suites, and iterative human review.
7. **Quantify Quality & Regressions:** Build deterministic evaluation harnesses combining rule-based checks and calibrated LLM-as-a-Judge scoring.
8. **Trace & Debug Locally:** Instrument multi-step agent runs with zero-friction local OpenTelemetry and Langfuse tracing to pinpoint latency and cost bottlenecks.
9. **Harden Against Threats:** Red-team tool-using agents against direct and indirect prompt injection, applying least privilege and deterministic approval gates.
10. **Formulate Adoption Roadmaps:** Draft enterprise-grade governance, data privacy, and IP protection guidelines for deploying agents in real-world organizations.

### Detailed Daily Curriculum

#### Day 1 &middot; Foundations & Core Architecture

Day 1 transitions participants from single-prompt LLM calls to working, goal-directed agents, followed by an exploration of foundational patterns and framework selection.

##### Session 1 &middot; 09:00 &ndash; 10:30 &middot; What is Agentic AI?
- **Topics:**
  - Chatbots (conversational UI) vs. LLM Pipelines (static chains) vs. Autonomous Agents.
  - The Autonomy Spectrum: from deterministic scripts to autonomous multi-agent systems.
  - The Perceive-Reason-Act loop: Observation $\rightarrow$ Thought $\rightarrow$ Action $\rightarrow$ Environment Feedback.
  - Value vs. Risk: identifying genuine agentic use cases and when deterministic code is strictly superior.
- **Hands-on Lab 1:** Convert a single Gemini prompt call into an autonomous tool-using loop calling database lookup and calculation functions.

##### Session 2 &middot; 11:00 &ndash; 12:30 &middot; Anatomy of an Agent
- **Topics:**
  - The 5 core pillars: Model, System Instructions, Tool Contracts, Memory, and Control Loop.
  - Context Engineering: token budgeting, system prompt formulation, dynamic context injection, and mitigating context degradation.
  - Tool Design: rigorous JSON Schema generation via Pydantic v2, unambiguous descriptions, and error feedback as agent steering signals.
  - Memory architectures: short-term context scratchpad vs. persistent key-value and vector memory.
- **Hands-on Lab 2:** Build an agent runtime from scratch in raw Python (no third-party frameworks) with Pydantic tool schemas, conversational buffer, and error recovery.

##### Session 3 &middot; 14:00 &ndash; 15:30 &middot; Agentic System Types and Patterns
- **Topics:**
  - Deterministic Workflows vs. Autonomous Agents (predictability vs. dynamic flexibility).
  - Common patterns: Prompt Chaining, Routing, Parallelization (Voting & Sectioning), Orchestrator-Workers, and Evaluator-Optimizer loops.
  - Agentic RAG: Corrective RAG (CRAG), query rewriting, document relevance grading, and fallback search.
  - Designing with Occam’s Razor: choosing the simplest reliable pattern.
- **Hands-on Lab 3:** Implement two architectural patterns (sequential chain vs. orchestrator-worker) for technical document analysis and compare latency, cost, and output consistency.

##### Session 4 &middot; 16:00 &ndash; 17:30 &middot; Framework Landscape & Selection Matrix
- **Topics:**
  - Comparative analysis: **LangGraph**, **Google Gen AI ADK**, **CrewAI**, **AutoGen/AG2**, **OpenAI Agents SDK**, and **Claude Agent SDK**.
  - Decision criteria: control, learning curve, debugging ease, state persistence, ecosystem lock-in, and production readiness.
  - Framework vs. No-Framework: when to use a specialized framework vs. raw Python with FastAPI.
- **Group Activity 1:** Evaluate three real-world software engineering case studies (automated PR review & test fixer, customer support bot with actions, and data ingestion pipeline) and defend framework choices with a filled scorecard.

---

#### Day 2 &middot; Depth, Ecosystem & Tooling

Day 2 dives into production-grade frameworks, standard interoperability protocols, reusable capabilities, and developer productivity tools.

##### Session 5 &middot; 09:00 &ndash; 10:30 &middot; Framework Deep Dive: LangGraph & Google Gen AI ADK
- **Topics:**
  - **LangGraph**: State schemas (`TypedDict`), nodes, conditional edges, `MemorySaver` persistence, and the `interrupt()` human-in-the-loop mechanism.
  - **Google Gen AI ADK**: Declarative agent definitions, Gemini tool calling, runner lifecycles, and sub-agent delegation.
  - Comparing state management and human approval patterns across both frameworks.
- **Hands-on Lab 5:** Build a Technical Research Assistant in LangGraph and Google Gen AI ADK with Gemini that plans steps, searches documents, drafts an RFC, and pauses for human approval before committing.

##### Session 6 &middot; 11:00 &ndash; 12:30 &middot; Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- **Topics:**
  - The $N \times M$ integration problem and how MCP provides a universal standard.
  - Core architecture: Host $\leftrightarrow$ Client $\leftrightarrow$ Server.
  - The three MCP primitives: **Tools**, **Resources**, and **Prompts**.
  - Transports: Local (`stdio`) vs. Remote (`SSE` / HTTP with authentication).
  - MCP vs. Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocols vs. direct REST APIs.
- **Hands-on Lab 6:** Author a custom Python MCP server using `FastMCP` and `FastAPI` (with SSE and stdio transports) exposing a service catalog database, connect it to a Gemini agent client, and execute live queries.

##### Session 7 &middot; 14:00 &ndash; 15:30 &middot; Agent Skills & Progressive Disclosure
- **Topics:**
  - Anatomy of an Agent Skill: `SKILL.md` instruction contracts, scripts, references, and assets.
  - Progressive disclosure: keeping base context lean (~100 tokens per skill summary) and loading full instructions on-demand.
  - Conceptual boundaries: Skills vs. Tools vs. MCP Servers vs. Prompts.
  - Authoring, linting, testing, and distributing skills across developer teams.
- **Hands-on Lab 7:** Author a production skill (e.g., "API Contract & Security Auditor"), define trigger metadata, write verification test scripts, and test on sample inputs.

##### Session 8 &middot; 16:00 &ndash; 17:30 &middot; Coding Agents in Modern Engineering
- **Topics:**
  - How coding agents work: workspace indexing, bash execution, diff-based file editing, linter loops.
  - Spec-driven development: writing crisp requirement specifications, acceptance tests, and boundary constraints before agent execution.
  - Pitfalls and mitigations: hallucinated dependencies, subtle logic regressions, context pollution, unreviewed git changes.
- **Hands-on Lab 8:** Direct a coding agent via CLI to scaffold a FastAPI microservice, write unit tests with `pytest`, refactor with async rate-limiting, and verify test passes.

---

#### Day 3 &middot; Trust, Production & Enterprise Application

Day 3 turns working prototypes into trustworthy, production-grade systems through evaluation, zero-friction telemetry, security hardening, and governance.

##### Session 9 &middot; 09:00 &ndash; 10:30 &middot; Evaluation and Testing of Agentic Systems
- **Topics:**
  - Why testing agents is hard: non-deterministic outputs and stochastic multi-step paths.
  - Outcome evaluation (task success, schema adherence) vs. Trajectory evaluation (tool call efficiency, loop count, cost).
  - LLM-as-a-Judge: scoring rubrics, calibration, pairwise evaluations, mitigating position and verbosity bias.
  - Continuous regression testing and synthetic test datasets.
- **Hands-on Lab 9:** Build a 20-case test dataset with `pytest` and evaluate the Day 2 agent using both deterministic assertions and an automated Gemini LLM judge.

##### Session 10 &middot; 10:45 &ndash; 12:15 &middot; Observability, Tracing & Cost Engineering
- **Topics:**
  - Telemetry fundamentals: Traces, Spans, Events, and OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.
  - Zero-friction local setup: local SQLite trace logger and console/file exporters (with optional free Langfuse cloud).
  - Pinpointing failures: diagnosing infinite loops, tool errors, token blowouts, and latency bottlenecks.
  - Cost engineering: tracking tokens per turn, caching static contexts, and optimizing model tier selection.
- **Hands-on Lab 10:** Instrument the LangGraph / ADK agent with local tracing, inject a deliberate tool failure and token blowout, and diagnose the root cause using the waterfall trace view.

##### Session 11 &middot; 13:00 &ndash; 14:30 &middot; Security, Guardrails & Red-Teaming
- **Topics:**
  - Threat taxonomy: Direct prompt injection, indirect prompt injection (poisoned tool inputs), SSRF via web fetchers, tool parameter tampering, and unauthorized action execution.
  - MCP supply chain risks: untrusted servers and package vulnerabilities.
  - Defense-in-depth: Principle of least privilege, input/output validation, sandboxed execution, and approval gates.
  - OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications.
- **Hands-on Lab 11:** Red-team peer agents with prompt injection payloads; implement input filters and strict Pydantic parameter boundaries to harden against attacks.

##### Session 12 &middot; 14:45 &ndash; 15:45 &middot; Enterprise Governance & Responsible AI
- **Topics:**
  - Data privacy and Zero Data Retention (ZDR) policies with model providers.
  - IP safety and licensing considerations for agent-generated code and artifacts.
  - Audit logging, accountability, and enterprise adoption roadmaps.
  - Establishing an internal AI Center of Excellence (CoE) and operational SLAs.
- **Group Activity 2:** Draft an Enterprise Agentic AI Readiness Checklist and risk mitigation plan for an engineering team.

##### Capstone Showcase &middot; 16:00 &ndash; 17:30
- **Objective:** Consolidate all three days by building and demonstrating an end-to-end production-grade agent addressing an enterprise use case.
- **Requirements:**
  1. Stateful workflow using LangGraph or Google Gen AI ADK with Gemini.
  2. Custom MCP tool or resource integration.
  3. Deterministic human approval gate for state-mutating actions.
  4. Local OpenTelemetry / Langfuse trace demonstrating execution path.
  5. Automated evaluation scorecard with at least 5 test cases.
- **Deliverable:** Live demo, peer review, and a personal 30-day adoption roadmap.

### Local Environment & Setup Requirements

Each participant works on their own laptop with Python 3.11+, an isolated virtual environment managed by **`uv`**, Node.js 22 LTS, and a Google Gemini API key.

#### Hardware & Software Checklist

| Component | Minimum Specification | Recommended | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Operating System** | Windows 11, macOS 13+, or Ubuntu 22.04+ | Same, fully updated | Labs verified on all three platforms |
| **Memory (RAM)** | 8 GB RAM | 16 GB RAM or more | 16 GB recommended if running local Ollama models |
| **Free Disk Space** | 10 GB | 25 GB | For virtual environments, packages, and caching |
| **Python** | 3.11 or 3.12 | 3.12 via `uv` | Managed with `uv python install 3.12` |
| **Python Tooling** | `uv` package manager | Latest `uv` release | Ultra-fast dependency resolution and lockfiles |
| **Node.js** | Node.js 22 LTS | Node.js 22 LTS | Minimum Node 22 with `npm` for MCP servers |
| **Git & VS Code** | Current stable releases | VS Code with Python extension | For cloning repositories and editing code |
| **Docker (Optional)** | Docker Desktop | Current release | Optional for self-hosted Langfuse or sandboxing |
| **Model API Key** | Google Gemini API Key | Gemini 2.5 Flash / Pro | Active key configured in `.env` |

### Python Package Manifest (`pyproject.toml` / `uv`)

```toml
[project]
name = "agentic-ai-bootcamp"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Hands-on code and labs for the 3-Day Agentic AI Engineering Bootcamp"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "google-genai>=0.1.0",
    "langchain-google-genai>=2.0.0",
    "langgraph>=0.2.0",
    "langchain-core>=0.3.0",
    "mcp>=1.0.0",
    "pydantic>=2.9.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.5.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "fastapi>=0.115.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.31.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.1",
    "pytest>=8.3.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.24.0",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.27.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.27.0",
    "langfuse>=2.50.0",
    "pip-audit>=2.7.3",
]
```

#### Quick Setup Steps with `uv`

```bash
# 1. Ensure uv is installed
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# 2. Clone the repository and initialize environment
git clone <bootcamp-repo-url> agentic-bootcamp
cd agentic-bootcamp
uv sync

# 3. Configure API Keys
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env and set: GEMINI_API_KEY="your-gemini-api-key"

# 4. Verify environment with check script
uv run python scripts/check_env.py
```

The `check_env.py` script validates the Python version, Node.js version, package imports, and executes a test ping to the Google Gemini API to ensure complete readiness before Day 1.

### Participant Deliverables & Assessment

Every participant leaves the bootcamp with complete, tested artifacts:
1. **Lab Code Repository:** Executable code for all 10 hands-on labs.
2. **Framework Decision Matrix:** Customized evaluation scorecard for their team's use cases.
3. **Custom MCP Server & Skill:** Working MCP server and packaged reusable skill bundle.
4. **Automated Evaluation Set:** 20-case test dataset with outcome and trajectory scoring.
5. **Security & Guardrails Checklist:** Hardened agent configuration and threat audit template.
6. **Capstone Project:** Complete, working production-grade agent with telemetry and human gates.
7. **30-Day Adoption Roadmap:** Personal or team action plan for scaling agentic AI.
